name: Kettlebell Swing
summary: A ballistic hip-hinge exercise that develops explosive posterior chain power, conditioning, and core stability using a kettlebell.

setup: Place the kettlebell on the floor about one foot in front of you.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at the hips with soft knees, reaching forward to grip the kettlebell handle with both hands using an overhand grip.
Tilt the kettlebell slightly back toward you while engaging your lats and keeping your spine neutral.
steps: Hike the kettlebell dynamically back between your upper thighs, keeping your forearms connected to your inner thighs.
Snap your hips forward violently and contract your glutes and core to drive the kettlebell upward.
Allow the kettlebell to float freely to roughly chest height, keeping your arms relaxed like ropes.
Let gravity guide the kettlebell back down into the hinge; wait until your forearms contact your torso before hinging your hips back to absorb the load for the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Inhale sharply as you hike the bell back into the hinge, and exhale forcefully through pursed lips as you snap your hips into full extension.
cues: Pop the hips, don't lift with the arms
Stand tall at the top like a plank

common_faults.fault: Squatting the weight rather than hinging at the hips.
common_faults.correction: Push the hips backward and keep the shins relatively vertical with minimal knee bend.

common_faults.fault: Using the shoulders and arms to raise the kettlebell.
common_faults.correction: Treat the arms as tethers; all upward momentum must come from the violent hip extension.

common_faults.fault: Hinging too early on the descent.
common_faults.correction: Wait to hinge until the kettlebell has descended near hip height and the upper arms touch the ribs.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the peak of the swing.
common_faults.correction: Finish in a solid vertical plank position by bracing your abs and squeezing the glutes without leaning back.

precautions: Ensure clear space in front of and behind you.
Never use slippery hands or loose grip; use chalk if needed.
Park the kettlebell safely by letting it swing back between the legs and setting it down out in front, rather than stopping abruptly.
